name: Museum communications editor
scenario: A bilingual museum editor adapts public copy for different audiences. Proofing approved bilingual copy is usually quick, while a short passage can be slow when the glossary or intended audience changes.

tasks.title: Revisar doce cartelas de la colección
tasks.description: Compare the approved Spanish and English labels for punctuation, inventory numbers, and accent marks. Return a marked PDF.
tasks.details: Translations and terminology were signed off last week. Preserve artwork titles exactly.

tasks.title: Adapt the ceramics panel for school visits
tasks.description: Prepare a Spanish panel for readers aged 9–12 using the English curatorial text. Retain object names and the distinction between firing and glazing.
tasks.details: The draft is short. Replace unexplained technical vocabulary and fit text into the existing panel.

pdf.title: Gallery school visit: bilingual panel brief

sections.heading: Curatorial draft
sections.body: After the first firing, the vessel was coated with a mineral mixture. A second firing fused that coat to the surface. A break near the foot reveals that the color and the underlying clay are different materials.

sections.heading: Audience and terminology
sections.body: Write for children visiting with a teacher. Define the two firings without implying the vessel was painted after its final firing. Retain the object label 'Vasija de dos asas' in the Spanish version.

sections.heading: Production constraints
sections.body: The English label is reference material. Write a new Spanish panel with a short headline and two short paragraphs. Provide one optional spoken prompt for the guide and check the line breaks against the panel mock-up.

tasks.title: Proofread the spring hours notice
tasks.description: Verify two English and Spanish listings against the approved schedule and fix any mismatched day names.
tasks.details: Use el museo for the institution. The new notice follows the winter template.

tasks.title: Rewrite an audio-guide stop in plain Spanish
tasks.description: Make a 90-second spoken script from the curator's long English label. Keep the object description usable for a listener who cannot see the case.
tasks.details: Try the script aloud, leave breathing room at line breaks, and avoid directional words such as over here.

tasks.title: Update the bilingual event calendar
tasks.description: Proof the dates, location names and accents on six already translated event listings.
tasks.details: Check the events sheet and the official accent list; no copy changes requested.

tasks.title: Resolve the craft glossary before translation
tasks.description: Prepare a bilingual shortlist for six tool names and flag the entries that need a curator's decision.
tasks.details: Two names are regional. Include a one-sentence usage example for each candidate.

tasks.title: Translate the member newsletter paragraph
tasks.description: Translate the general welcome and two practical reminders. Reuse approved membership terminology and preserve links.
tasks.details: Audience is regular members. The spring events already have official bilingual names.

holdouts.title: Prepare Spanish text for the weaving stop
holdouts.description: Turn the curator's source into copy that a visiting child can follow and that the designer can fit on the panel.
holdouts.details: Use the attached layout brief and keep the approved object name.

sections.heading: Source passage
sections.body: The shuttle takes the weft through a temporary opening in the warp. By changing which threads rise, the weaver builds a pattern. The striped sampler preserves three attempts at the same repeat, with the last repeat reversed.

sections.heading: Audience instruction
sections.body: The visitor will be holding a cardboard loom and following one step at a time. Write the body in Spanish. Introduce urdimbre and trama once, each with a short explanation a child could understand.

sections.heading: Handoff
sections.body: Deliver a 45-word panel and a 20-second guide prompt. Preserve the name Muestrario de franjas. Check which explanation is intelligible when read aloud; the designer cannot add a diagram.

holdouts.check: Tests multilingual semantic comparison and audience adaptation when the clearest historical match discusses a different craft.

holdouts.title: Proof the English and Spanish visitor map
holdouts.description: Check spelling and accents in the six bilingual facility labels and fix the new Sunday closing time.
holdouts.details: The translations have approval. The copy can be edited in an existing two-column document.
holdouts.check: Select approved bilingual proofreading examples and check whether the model overcorrects an already well-budgeted edit.
